In which section of the Calloways' inves.Return requirement: This section states the target return (absolute or relative, before or after tax and inflation), not cash the clients must be able to reach.
In which section of the Calloways' inves.Laws and regulations: For individuals this section is usually minor; it matters mainly for retirement plans or endowments subject to rules such as ERISA.
In which section of the Calloways' inves.Permitted and excluded investments: This section lists holdings the clients want included or ruled out (for example, for social or religious reasons), not near-term cash needs.

Which statement best describes the Callo.Low ability and low willingness; the IPS: Their wealth, income, insurance and 12-year horizon give them a high ability to take risk, and a goal needing 6.5% cannot simply stay unchanged under a capital-preservation mix.
Which statement best describes the Callo.High ability and high willingness; their: Graham’s panic selling and fear of a 15% drop show low willingness, which the IPS must address rather than ignore.
Which statement best describes the Callo.Low ability but high willingness; the pl: Ability is high, not low, and a questionnaire score alone ignores the behavior Graham has already shown.

How large is the gap in the Calloways' e.$19,000; arrange a 401(k) loan that can: A retirement-plan loan is borrowing, not a reserve; a liquid money market holding is the preferred way to meet an unexpected crisis.
How large is the gap in the Calloways' e.$81,000; open a home equity line of cred: $81,000 is the full target, not the gap, and a credit line is borrowing, not a liquid reserve the clients own.
How large is the gap in the Calloways' e.$39,000; leave the CD out of the reserve: A bank CD is a cash equivalent that can be redeemed (at most with an interest penalty), so excluding it overstates the gap, and 401(k) money is not a reserve.

Which response by the planner is most ac.She is right; both accounts carry FDIC c: Only the bank MMDA is FDIC insured; a money market mutual fund is an investment company product without federal insurance.
Which response by the planner is most ac.She is right only if the fund holds Trea: Holding Treasury bills improves a fund’s credit quality but does not give the fund FDIC coverage.
Which response by the planner is most ac.Neither account is insured, but only the: The MMDA is federally insured, and money market mutual funds also commonly allow withdrawals by check.

What is the Calloways' after-tax, inflat.0.97%: 0.97% is the pre-tax real return (1.04 ÷ 1.03 − 1); it ignores federal tax on the interest.
What is the Calloways' after-tax, inflat.1.00%: 1.00% just subtracts inflation from the nominal yield and ignores both tax and the proper real-return formula.
What is the Calloways' after-tax, inflat.&minus;0.47%: This applies the 5% state rate as well, but T-bill interest is exempt from state income tax.

What is the planner's best course of act.Move the 401(k) to stable value now and: Waiting for a partial recovery is market timing; it tends to miss the early part of a rebound and locks in the loss.
What is the planner's best course of act.Shift half the 401(k) to stable value as: Cutting stocks by half still reacts to the market rather than to any change in the clients’ goals, horizon or resources.
What is the planner's best course of act.Rewrite the IPS around capital preservat: The decline does not change their goals, horizon, jobs or reserves; the IPS exists to keep them from reacting to this kind of turmoil.

Which event(s) should prompt the planner.I and III: A 4% raise is incremental change: worth monitoring, but not a reason to redesign the IPS.
Which event(s) should prompt the planner.II and III: A one-week 2% dip is market noise, which the IPS is designed to help clients ignore.
Which event(s) should prompt the planner.I, II, and III: Only the layoff is a discontinuous change; the raise is incremental and the dip is noise.

Which approach best reconciles the spous.Tactical asset allocation applied to the: TAA shifts the whole mix on market views, with high turnover and costs, the opposite of Graham’s low-cost, low-trading wish.
Which approach best reconciles the spous.A single moderate model portfolio from a: A sponsor model is a one-size-fits-all black box that ignores Nadia’s specific wish for an active sleeve.
Which approach best reconciles the spous.A strategic allocation held entirely in: An all-index portfolio satisfies Graham but gives Nadia no active satellite at all.

Which strategy best meets Nadia's goals.Transfer the shares to a charitable rema: A CRT can sell without tax and creates a deduction, but the remainder goes to charity, contrary to her wish to keep the value in the family.
Which strategy best meets Nadia's goals.Give the shares to Leah and Sam: A gift removes the shares from her control and may raise gift-tax issues; it moves the concentration rather than diversifying it.
Which strategy best meets Nadia's goals.Sell the shares and buy a diversified in: Selling diversifies but triggers capital gains tax right away on a $200,000 gain (4,000 × $50).

Ignoring commissions, what is the minimu.$300,000: This subtracts the premium twice (as if the floor were $75 a share); the floor is $80 × 4,000 less the $10,000 premium once.
Ignoring commissions, what is the minimu.$320,000: $320,000 is the strike value but ignores the $10,000 paid for the puts.
Ignoring commissions, what is the minimu.$350,000: This subtracts the premium from today’s value, not from the $80 strike floor.

Which option position should Nadia add t.Write 40 $105 covered calls and nothing: Covered calls earn income and cap the upside, but the premium gives only a small cushion if KDX falls sharply.
Which option position should Nadia add t.Write 40 $80 puts and buy 40 $105 calls: Writing puts adds a duty to buy more KDX if it falls, and buying calls adds upside exposure: the reverse of a hedge.
Which option position should Nadia add t.Buy 40 $90 calls and 40 $90 puts (a long: A long straddle bets on a big move either way and costs two premiums; it is not a no-cost floor.

Using the CAPM, what is the required ret.18.0%; KDX is undervalued, so buy more: 18.0% multiplies the whole market return by beta (4% + 10% × 1.4) instead of only the market risk premium.
Using the CAPM, what is the required ret.8.4%; the expected return exceeds it, so: 8.4% is only the stock’s risk premium (6% × 1.4); the risk-free rate must be added back.
Using the CAPM, what is the required ret.14.0%; KDX plots on the security market: 14.0% is market return × beta with no risk-free intercept, and an asset on the SML would have expected return equal to required return, which is not the case.

What is the weighted beta of the equity.1.15: 1.15 is the simple average of the three betas; it ignores that KDX is 75% of the dollars.
What is the weighted beta of the equity.1.40: 1.40 is KDX’s beta alone; the two funds pull the weighted figure down.
What is the weighted beta of the equity.1.07: 1.07 weights only the two funds and leaves out the KDX shares.

Using the R² threshold taught in the cou.Large-Cap Value Index, R² = 0.88: An R² of 0.88 means 88% of its movement tracks the S&P 500; it largely duplicates the index fund.
Using the R² threshold taught in the cou.Mid-Cap Blend, R² = 0.79: 0.79 is above the 70% threshold, so it moves too closely with the S&P 500 to diversify well.
Using the R² threshold taught in the cou.Dividend Growth, R² = 0.74: 0.74 is still above 70%; a correlation of 0.86 exceeds the roughly 0.84 cutoff.

Which fund shows the better risk-adjuste.Bexley, because its Treynor ratio (7.50): Treynor relies on beta, and Bexley’s R² of 0.58 makes its beta unreliable, so its Treynor edge cannot be trusted.
Which fund shows the better risk-adjuste.Bexley, because its return is 1.4 points: Raw return ignores risk; Bexley earned its extra return with far higher volatility.
Which fund shows the better risk-adjuste.Alder, because its higher R² shows it ha: A higher R² only means the fund tracks the market more closely; it is not a measure of risk-adjusted performance or skill.

Which of these statements about Harborli.I and III: Statement III is false (the expense ratio excludes brokerage commissions), and this choice leaves out true statements II and IV.
Which of these statements about Harborli.II and IV: II and IV are true, but so is I: trading costs from turnover sit outside the expense ratio.
Which of these statements about Harborli.I, II, III, and IV: III is false; the expense ratio covers operating expenses, management fees and 12b-1 fees, not the fund’s brokerage commissions.

What loss can the Calloways recognize on.$15,000 loss; basis $82,000: The loss cannot be recognized because the same fund was bought back within 30 days, and the new basis must absorb the disallowed loss.
What loss can the Calloways recognize on.$3,000 loss; basis $94,000: $3,000 is the annual cap on deducting net capital losses (2026 edition figure); here the whole loss is postponed by the wash-sale rule.
What loss can the Calloways recognize on.$0 loss; basis $82,000: The disallowed $15,000 is not forfeited; it is added to the new shares’ basis, making it $97,000.

What is the municipal fund's taxable-equ.5.29%; the municipal fund: 5.29% uses only the federal rate; for an in-state bond exempt from both taxes, the state rate must be included.
What is the municipal fund's taxable-equ.5.71%; the municipal fund: Adding the two brackets (37%) is the shortcut for taxpayers who do not itemize; the Calloways itemize.
What is the municipal fund's taxable-equ.5.57%; the corporate fund: The TEY is right but the conclusion is wrong: 5.57% beats the corporate fund’s 5.2%, so the municipal fund wins after tax.

Which change makes the Calloways' asset.Buy municipal bonds inside Nadia&rsquo;s: Municipal interest is already tax-exempt, so holding munis in a Roth wastes the account’s shelter on income that needed none.
Which change makes the Calloways' asset.Keep the bond fund in the joint account,: Interest in a taxable account is taxed every year; inside a 401(k) it is deferred, so location matters.
Which change makes the Calloways' asset.Swap the bond fund for taxable zero-coup: Taxable zero-coupon bonds create phantom income (accrued interest taxed yearly), so they also belong in tax-deferred accounts.

Using the duration formula, approximatel.$56,280: This uses the rule of thumb (6.2 × 1%) and skips dividing by 1 + YTM, which the formula requires.
Using the duration formula, approximatel.$63,536: The sign is backward; bond prices fall when rates rise.
Using the duration formula, approximatel.$59,400: This drops the value by only the 1% rate change and ignores the duration multiplier.

Which fixed-income approach best protect.A long-term bond fund with a duration of: A duration of 14 is far longer than the 3-year horizon, so a rise in rates before tuition is due could cut the value sharply.
Which fixed-income approach best protect.A barbell of 1-year and 20-year bonds: A barbell needs active management and its long end carries large price risk; it does not lock in a value on a set date.
Which fixed-income approach best protect.Keep the stock index fund, since stocks: With only three years left, a bear market could shrink the fund just before it is needed; near-term goals belong outside stocks.

What was the Calloways' holding period r.9.00%: 9% is the return in euros; it ignores that each euro now converts into fewer dollars than at purchase.
What was the Calloways' holding period r.15.41%: 15.41% inverts the exchange-rate change, treating the dollar’s rise as a gain for a U.S. holder of euro assets.
What was the Calloways' holding period r.3.44%: 3.44% subtracts the currency loss from the local return instead of compounding the two (1.09 × 0.9444 − 1).
